First fix the source of the leak. Then...

  • Wear a mask. Do not breathe in bleach vapors.
  • Wear gloves. It will do a number on your hands.
  • Make a bleach solution of 1 part bleach to 8 parts water. Add 8 drops of dish washing liquid. This acts as a surfactant to penetrate.
  • Open up the walls (if they aren't already) and remove all the drywall that has mold, and discard it.
  • For other things you cannot discard, like framing, pipes, etc, wipe down with a sponge with that bleach solution. Get every nook and cranny, use a spray bottle to lightly spray the solution on and rub it in. Throw away any furniture or carpet that got wet, just get rid of any possible source of mold you can.
  • Dry area thoroughly. Use a room dehumidifier if you have one. To get into cracks that may not get much air circulation use a hair dryer to dry them. Make sure ALL the damp is gone.
  • During the few days it's drying make sure you didn't miss a secondary source of a leak.
  • After 7 days, patch up the wall.

NOTES:

  • Make sure air is being pulled out of the basement and replaced with fresh air. This air circulation will help dry the basement.
  • Natural gas heaters in the basement produce some water vapor so make sure this is not a source of moisture via condensation.
